title: 4-bit parallel-access shift register

sources.document: TI The TTL Data Book for Design Engineers, 2nd ed. (1981), TYPES SN5495A, SN54L95, SN54LS95B, SN7495A, SN74L95, SN74LS95B 4-bit parallel-access shift registers, bulletin DL-S 7611872 (March 1974, revised October 1976; LS95B page revised December 1980)

pins.name: SER
pins.text: serial input (shift right enters here into QA)

pins.name: MODE
pins.text: mode control: high = parallel load (and shift left) on clock 2, low = shift right on clock 1

pins.name: CK2
pins.text: clock 2, left shift / load; acts on its high-to-low edge while MODE is high

pins.name: CK1
pins.text: clock 1, right shift; acts on its high-to-low edge while MODE is low

state.changesOn: falling edge of CK2 (MODE high) or of CK1 (MODE low)
rules: MODE high, CK2 falls: QA-QD = A-D (parallel load)
MODE low, CK1 falls: shift right, QA = SER, QB = old QA, QC = old QB, QD = old QC
MODE high: CK1 has no effect; MODE low: CK2 has no effect
Shift left is a parallel load with QB wired to A, QC to B, QD to C and serial data at D
MODE should normally change only while both clocks are low; the last five lines of the function table show the other cases where the register still holds

timing.conditions: VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, RL 2 kohm, CL 15 pF
VCC 5 V, TA 25 C, RL 2 kohm, CL 15 pF

unknown: Figure 2 (the waveform that defines the enable/inhibit times) was not read; the reference edges of those four limits are not settled.
Pin names SER, MODE, CK1, CK2 are short forms of the datasheet's SERIAL INPUT, MODE CONTROL, CLOCK 1 R-SHIFT and CLOCK 2 L-SHIFT (LOAD).
notes: Exact-name file: the family rule cannot reach a type that ends in a letter. The book also shows SN7495A and SN74L95 on the same pages; those figures are not in this file.
